walkthroughs.body_html:
Power tells you how fast energy is transferred. 💡

P = I × V works for any component. For a resistor you can also use P = I² × R or P = V² ÷ R.

Units: watts (W). 1 W = 1 J per second.

Energy transferred: E = P × t. In joules if t is in seconds.

Electricity bills use the kilowatt-hour (kWh): power in kW times time in hours. A 2 kW heater on for 3 hours uses 6 kWh.

Cost = energy in kWh × price per kWh.

A fixed resistor at constant temperature gives a straight line through the origin — it is ohmic.

A filament lamp heats up, so resistance rises — the line curves and flattens.

A diode only conducts one way — current is zero in reverse. An LDR resistance falls as light rises.

mcqs.q: A 230 V kettle draws 10 A. What is its power?
The I-V graph of a filament lamp is a curve that flattens out. Why?
options: Its resistance increases as it heats up

numericals.q: A 2 kW electric heater is on for 3 hours. The energy company charges 30 p per kWh. What is the cost, in pence?
numericals.hint: Energy in kWh = power (kW) × time (h). Then multiply by price.

free_texts.q: A current of 4 A flows through a 5 Ω resistor. What is the power dissipated, in watts? Give a number only.
